prompt: `caesar` is meant to handle any shift, including negative ones. Shifting by -3 sends `d` to the wrong place. Tap the faulty line.
explain: In C, `%` keeps the sign of the left operand, so `-3 % 26` is -3, and the sum under the second `%` can go negative too. Adding 26 before the final `% 26` -- `((shift % 26) + 26) % 26` -- always gives 0 to 25.
